text:
Maya: heads-up — we're seeing a sharp retry/spike window on model-serving in us-west-2 starting ~09:12. 502s + per-pod GPU queue growth. Seems east-west traffic is getting fragmented and some endpoints are getting almost all connections. Anyone oncall?

Sam: same. tcp retransmits, app logs show connection retries and ipvs counters are extremely lopsided. quick `ipvsadm -Ln --sort` snapshot: 
```
TCP  0.0.0.0:443 rr  masq
  -> 10.10.5.21:443      Masq    1000     9000
  -> 10.10.5.22:443      Masq    12       8
  -> 10.10.5.23:443      Masq    9        6
```
This is the pattern across several services.

Maya: I ran tcpdump on a couple of pods — large segments with DF set and then ICMP fragmentation-needed / PMTU blackhole-like behavior. RDMA nodes show MSS mismatch on the veth side. Looks like encapsulation (VXLAN) + GSO/GRO are producing fragments the kernel/IPVS isn't handling consistently. @Priya can you check tunnel MTU/encap settings?

Priya: I rolled GRO/GSO/TOS off on one suspected node: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` — immediate drop in retries and traffic rebalanced across endpoints. :white_check_mark: But of course that hits throughput. This suggests offloads + tunneled MTU is the trigger.

Jules: wonder if kube-proxy/ipvs sync heuristics prefer the non-fragmented path and end up hot-sharding one endpoint. We can try bumping `--ipvs-sync-period` to force faster rebalancing, but that feels like papering over. Also consider conntrack table pressure — retransmits + new handshakes create churn.

Maya: temporary mitigation: cordoned the worst host and drained, disabled large offloads on remaining tunneled nodes. Planning a rolling kube-proxy restart with `--ipvs-sync-period=5s` for the next hour as a low-risk step. Will monitor latencies and per-endpoint tx/rx.

InfraBot: Incident INC-2026-045 created, priority P2. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/ipvs-frag-mtu. Logs uploaded to /var/log/infra/ipvs/2155001234.log.

Sam: long term we should standardize MTU on physical hosts -> tunnel interfaces -> pod veths (9000 everywhere or 1450 everywhere), and ensure GSO/GRO semantics are correct for encrypted tunnels. Also file kernel bug for VXLAN+GSO interaction.

Priya: actionables: 1) stage change to align VXLAN MTU to 9000 on staging cluster and run perf tests, 2) add alert: "endpoint_hit_rate_skew > 60% for 5m"; 3) add RDMA/eth counters to node exporter. I can take 1 and 2.

Maya: thanks. TL;DR for postmortem: IPVS route selection + segmented fragments from offload+tunnel MTU mismatch caused uneven endpoint distribution and retry spike; mitigations = disable offload on tunnel endpoints (short-term), standardize MTU and fix kernel handling (long-term). Filed kernel bug/cc:netdev.

Jules: +1 on postmortem. also recommend a canary change to kube-proxy flags in staging before rolling.

Priya: will report back with staging results in ~2h.

Maya: ping if you see any recurrence. Thanks all. :rocket:
